core_obligations: The two morphisms of sites (proof lines 6637-6643): the companion proposition applies to the given functor, and the induced functor on the localized sites also satisfies its assumptions, so both morphisms of sites exist.

Commutativity (proof lines 6644-6651): the diagram commutes by the definition of composition of morphisms of sites, because the functor commutes with finite limits, which makes the opposite diagram of categories and functors commutative.
proof_roadmap: Apply the companion proposition to the given functor and to the induced functor on the localized sites.
Check that the induced functor again satisfies the assumptions.
Use commutation with finite limits and the definition of composition to get the commutative diagram.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a commutative diagram of morphisms of sites between the localizations when the functor is continuous and commutes with finite limits, identifies it with the diagram obtained from the localizations of the sites, and records the resulting identity for the pushforward (statement lines 6604-6634). The proof is short and complete: the companion proposition produces both morphisms of sites, since the induced functor on the localized sites satisfies the same assumptions (proof lines 6637-6643); and the commutativity follows from the definition of composition together with the commutation of the functor with finite limits, displayed explicitly (proof lines 6644-6651). The non-formal content is the verification that the induced functor satisfies the assumptions. The claim is H1: two short steps with each input named.
